newsitem.title: FRANCE: France holds Spanish Basque for recruiting for ETA.
newsitem.headline: France holds Spanish Basque for recruiting for ETA.

text.p: A French judge on Friday remanded in custody a Spanish Basque woman suspected of having recruited two French Basque men as courriers for the guerrilla group ETA (Basque Homeland and Freedom), justice sources said.
Miren Magi Perurena Pascual, 25, was formally placed under investigation on suspicion of conspiracy to terrorism.
The two men, Iker Elizalde and Heren Muruaga, both with dual French and Spanish citizenship, were detained earlier this week in Paris.
Justice sources said ETA's attempt to recruit French citizens was a worrying development, indicating the group may be considering taking its violent campaign for a separate Basque state to France.

ETA, which has killed some 800 people in three decades, has so far limited its fight to Spain. But Spanish media recently said police had found ETA plans to kill a French military officer in Bordeaux, where French Prime Minister Alain Juppe is mayor.

French police, who have been stepping up a crackdown on ETA guerrillas sheltering in France, say they have found a list of potential French targets, including Interior Minister Jean-Louis Debre, but have not found any precise plans for attacks.
